races.name: Well Of Moate Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Earthwatch
runners_data.note: Posted four consecutive fourths in bumpers on Good ground suggesting consistency without a winning move; a genuine hold-up operator forced into midfield by the density of closers in this field, which tempers the chance of delivering a sharp late effort over just 2m at this modest tempo.

runners_data.name: Calamint
runners_data.note: Hurdles debut for Adrian Murray after 92 days off; placed in bumpers on Good ground but the stable has just one runner in the past 14 days and the 92-day absence makes fitness a question mark — headgear noted, hold-up style suits if a strong pace develops, which it won't.

runners_data.name: Captain Hanley
runners_data.note: Placed at 2m-3m on Good and yielding — the trip suits — but a hold-up horse naturally suited to staying trips who is here compressed into midfield; the 2m distance on a moderate gallop actually works against the delivery of his finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Digby Bridge
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed for Barry Connell, who struck once from two entries in the past 14 days; unknown style (tagged U) means no positional read is possible, and the lightly-raced profile is a genuine wildcard that cannot be dismissed in a wide-open maiden.

runners_data.name: Facile Ocean
runners_data.note: Has placed three times at 19f on Good ground — the trip and going both suit — and while a natural hold-up type mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear, the form profile here is among the strongest of the hold-up contingent; Eoghan Finegan takes the 5lb claim.

runners_data.name: First Ascent
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy — always relevant — takes over for Gordon Elliott after a 18-day break; a hold-up type suited by Good ground, though the record shows a pull-up and two mid-field finishes in recent hurdle runs, and the modest gallop reduces the chance of a decisive late charge.

runners_data.name: Through The Storm
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner, last seen 580 days ago; returns to dictate at a pace entirely to their liking, and while the absence is a fitness concern, the role of uncontested leader on Good ground over 2m is the defining tactical asset in this race.

runners_data.name: Whoyougonnacall
runners_data.note: A prominent racer who tracked into third on Good ground at 18f last time — the profile suits the likely race shape well; Liam Quinlan's light-framed ride from a prominent position gives this runner a natural fit that most rivals in this field simply cannot match.

runners_data.name: Not In A Hurry
runners_data.note: Completely unknown quantity on debut for Aidan Anthony Howard, with headgear noted and a hold-up pedigree suggested by the trainer tag; like Digby Bridge, the absence of form cuts both ways — impossible to discount, equally impossible to quantify.

runners_data.name: Anns Getaway
runners_data.note: Flagged as a fade-in-finish type from a 140-day layoff; a true hold-up horse pushed into midfield by the redistribution effect, and the combination of a moderate gallop, the fading flag, and a long absence makes the chance difficult to construct confidently.

runners_data.name: Rose Mountain
runners_data.note: Consistently poor recent form — P, 0, 0, 12, 16 — on Good ground over this trip; the fades-in-finish tag reinforces a pattern of non-staying, and the hold-up style on a modest pace over 2m is an uncomfortable combination given this profile.

races.paceDynamic: Through The Storm is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner maiden hurdle and, returning from a 580-day absence, will likely dictate from the front at a pace entirely of their own choosing — creating a controlled, single-file procession that is unlikely to generate any genuine pressure in the early or middle stages. Whoyougonnacall offers the only realistic prominent cover, tracking closely enough to keep Through The Storm honest but not to force a genuine test. This field holds significantly more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Earthwatch, Facile Ocean, Captain Hanley, Anns Getaway, and First Ascent are all true hold-up types redistributed to midfield, meaning several will be forced to race closer to the pace than they would prefer, compromising their ability to deliver a late challenge. The sustainable, uncontested gallop set by Through The Storm strongly favours any horse capable of tracking the leader in the prominent-to-midfield berths and picking off a tiring pacemaker in the home straight, rather than hold-up horses asked to make ground on a relatively modest tempo over just 2m.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Through The Storm dictates an uncontested moderate gallop and is collared in the final flight by a horse travelling prominently.
scenarios.body: Through The Storm sets a sedate pace with Whoyougonnacall tracking, and a horse held up in a forward position conserves enough energy to sweep past at the last; the modest tempo means class and jumping accuracy determine the finish rather than stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Through The Storm's 580-day break has left them fitter than expected and the modest gallop means they simply aren't run at hard enough to be caught.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to apply pressure until the home turn, Through The Storm dictates every yard and has enough in reserve to hold on; a field of hold-up horses struggling for their natural position fail to close the gap in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the modest pace causes compaction and a genuine hold-up horse finds a gap late to finish with purpose.
scenarios.body: One of the redistributed hold-up types — most likely Facile Ocean or Captain Hanley — manages to secure a clean run from the home turn and finish powerfully into a slowly-run race, catching a tiring leader and a prominent horse who has over-committed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Quantity Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly-raced, unknown-style debutants — Digby Bridge or Not In A Hurry — possesses sufficient raw ability to override any positional disadvantage.
scenarios.body: With no form to dissect, Digby Bridge or Not In A Hurry travel powerfully from an undemanding pace and show enough class to put experienced rivals to the sword; their unknown profiles become an asset rather than a liability in a modest maiden.

watchPoints.text: Through The Storm sets the entire tempo unchallenged — watch whether John Shinnick elects to use the 580-day layoff as a reason to coast or whether the horse shows sufficient freshness to lengthen at the last.

Whoyougonnacall is the only natural prominent type positioned to capitalise directly on the slow pace — watch whether Liam Quinlan tracks Through The Storm closely enough to pounce at the second-last or is tempted to move too early.

Facile Ocean, Captain Hanley, and Earthwatch are all true hold-up horses compressed into midfield — watch for a traffic-jam effect on the home turn if they all simultaneously seek a gap, potentially costing one of them a placing.

Digby Bridge and Not In A Hurry are unknown quantities making debuts — watch the betting market and paddock behaviour for any late clues about how these unexposed horses are expected to race by their connections.

The going is confirmed Good throughout the card at Kilbeggan — no late ground deterioration expected, so watch for horses whose form profiles are specifically built on Good ground (Facile Ocean, Earthwatch, Whoyougonnacall) to run their true race.

races.name: Kieran Kelly Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Liceo
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer for Dermot McLoughlin who has placed twice in similar-going tests over this trip; 25 days since last run is fine, tongue-tie applied, but the 0W2P record on Good ground and a back-of-field style in a race with minimal true pace makes the run to the line look awkward.

runners_data.name: Blue Reed
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner here under Jack Kennedy for Cian Collins; won over 19f on Good and has the course profile to slot straight to the front, but the STYLE_FIT flag at 0.93 signals it is operating outside its most comfortable role — still the most important horse tactically in this race.

runners_data.name: Syosset
runners_data.note: Five-pound claimer Michael Kenneally rides this McConnell-trained five-year-old who ran just five days ago; three placings in last three completed starts over similar distances on Good ground suggest genuine consistency, and a natural hold-up style that keeps it fresh for the finish suits if pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Valsorpresa
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old trained by Richard Daniels who has run over this exact going type in all 15 sampled starts; despite genuine hold-up tendencies, it will be pushed into a midfield slot by the volume of similar runners behind — the 0.93 STYLE_FIT discount is relevant to its winning prospects here.

runners_data.name: Walk Win
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for John Burke who holds a prominent tag and has a ⚠ fade-in-finish flag — handled Good ground twice placing second — but the tendency to empty late over this distance means any positional advantage gained up front may not last to the line.

runners_data.name: Folk Warrior
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old for J A Nash with very limited hurdles form (no wins, no places on Good ground in five sampled runs); comes off a flat career and the step up to 2m hurdles on Good at Kilbeggan represents an uncertain ask, though the unexposed angle holds mild interest in a scramble.

runners_data.name: Convincing
runners_data.note: Five-year-old for Ciaran Murphy whose flat form was over much shorter (8-10f) and whose hurdles debut over 16f on Soft was unimpressive; by nature a hold-up horse pushed into a midfield mapping here, and the STYLE_FIT tag at 0.92 reflects real doubts about this being his race shape.

runners_data.name: Zaryagle
runners_data.note: 293 days off the track for P J Rothwell's five-year-old, and its one Good-ground sample over 16f produced a sixth — a true rear-of-field runner who will find the compressed midfield even more suffocating given the long layoff and likely ring-rustiness.

runners_data.name: Corkbeg
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old for David Harry Kelly with 14 of 15 sampled runs on Good ground, so the surface is no issue; a natural hold-up type whose recent form reads 3-2 at longer distances — the step back to 2m may not fully suit, and the field's density means clean passage to the lead is far from guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Ferdia
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran for John Patrick Ryan whose form over 19-24f on Good ground is modest at best (7th, 8th, 6th); naturally races from the rear, and being mapped into a midfield cluster rather than his preferred position is an accurate reflection of what will happen in this race — difficult to win from here.

runners_data.name: Bravemans Bounce
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for Cian Collins returning after 85 days off; three runs total with no wins or places on Good ground, and the ⚠ fade-in-finish flag alongside the STYLE_FIT discount at 0.90 compounds a lean profile — likely to find this competitive field too much at this stage of its development.

runners_data.name: Kinski
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for J P Broderick back after 118 days; primarily a Soft/Heavy ground performer with only one of five sampled runs on Good — the going may not play to his strengths, and the fade-in-finish flag makes the long break into a harder surface a difficult combination.

runners_data.name: Ardgillan
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for M M Lynch returning after 245 days, with all five recent sampled runs on Soft or Heavy ground — the Good surface at Kilbeggan is a genuine question mark, and the fade-in-finish flag alongside the layoff makes this a significant risk even before accounting for the midfield redistribution.

runners_data.name: Surviving Murmansk
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old for James Barcoe who ran just five days ago; two wins from 15 Good-ground starts and placed third last time over 17f on Good suggests live each-way claims if the pace collapses late — a true hold-up runner whose recent confidence and fitness from the quick return partially offset the positional disadvantage.

races.paceDynamic: Blue Reed is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner field and, with no rival likely to dispute the lead aggressively, should bowl along at a comfortable, self-selected gallop over the 2m trip on Good ground at Kilbeggan. The pace will be genuine but not suicidal — Blue Reed sets an honest tempo that keeps the race together rather than stringing it out, meaning the field travels in a compact bunch through the early and middle stages. With only Syosset and Liceo carrying any real hold-up credentials at the rear, the bulk of this field will be competing for midfield positions, creating a congested, uniform shape that makes it difficult for true closers to find clean daylight late. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or pace-tracking profile — any horse capable of sitting just behind Blue Reed and travelling fluently into the straight holds the decisive positional edge. Several runners listed as redistributed — including Valsorpresa, Convincing, Zaryagle, Corkbeg, Ferdia, Bravemans Bounce, Kinski, Ardgillan, and Surviving Murmansk — are true hold-up types who will struggle to get their natural rear position given the volume of similarly-minded runners, with Blue Reed and Walk Win most likely to actually secure the front-end positions they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Blue Reed Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Reed jumps cleanly and immediately establishes a comfortable solo lead, dictating every yard of the 2m trip.
scenarios.body: Blue Reed bowls along at a manageable clip, the field strings out loosely behind, and the leader's stamina reserves are never tested by a rival for the lead; a prominent tracker who travels easily into the second half of the race can pick off any late weakener.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Reed's lead is modest enough that a fluent prominent-tracking type looms up turning for home and powers past before the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: A horse like Syosset, who has the form figures to travel prominently and finish, takes the lead approaching the last and holds any challenge from the moderate hold-up brigade who find themselves buried in midfield traffic.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Reed fades sharply after the second-last, gifting late-running types who thread through the field a genuine passage to the line.
scenarios.body: This outcome requires most of the redistributed hold-up horses to find clear daylight simultaneously, which is unlikely given field density, but Liceo or Surviving Murmansk — each with credible Good-ground form — could pick up the pieces if the pace genuinely collapses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Scrimmage Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed midfield causes interference at a hurdle, disrupting the race shape entirely and producing an unpredictable late-race lottery.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up types hunting the same ground through the back straight, a bunched run to the final flight could produce clipping and checking, opening the door for a horse like Folk Warrior or Convincing — relatively unexposed — to benefit from a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Blue Reed (Jack Kennedy) jumping from the front — if it flukes the lead and jumps cleanly throughout, the race is likely run entirely to its terms and no rival may get close enough to challenge before the last.

Congestion at the early hurdles is a real risk with 14 runners, the majority hunting the same midfield ground — Zaryagle, Ferdia, and Corkbeg are most likely to get shuffled wide or checked, compromising already modest winning chances.

Ardgillan and Kinski are both returning from very long breaks (245 and 118 days respectively) on ground conditions softer than their optimum — watch for early signs of ring-rustiness that could cause interference to nearby runners.

Surviving Murmansk ran just five days ago and comes here with freshness on its side despite the quick turnaround — if Blue Reed fades after the second-last, it is the hold-up runner best placed in terms of recent fitness to pick up the pieces.

Walk Win's fade-in-finish flag is worth monitoring from the front — if it pushes for early prominence and then empties between the last two hurdles, it could tighten up runners tracking it closely, particularly Syosset and Liceo coming from behind.

races.name: Joe Cooney Memorial Hurdle

runners_data.name: Drumgill
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner trained by John Patrick Ryan (same yard as Pets Georgina), who has no wins in 21 runners over 14 days; form includes a pulled-up run and inconsistency, but good-ground trips are familiar territory and 6 days since last run is fresh enough — will need the pace to truly collapse to get involved from this deep position.

runners_data.name: Olympic Man
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old confirmed front-runner taking on Rocky's Diamond at the head of affairs, but a 5lb claimer in the saddle, 29 days off, and a form string featuring a fall and a pulled-up run raise serious doubts about his ability to dominate; the tongue-tie is applied but he is likely to be pushed back from his natural lead role if Rocky's Diamond asserts.

runners_data.name: Rocky's Diamond
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner in the race at OR 148 and the most in-form runner through trainer angle (Queally 3/7 last 14 days); a natural front-runner who will contest the lead with Olympic Man, and his class advantage suggests he wins that battle — recent form over 22-24f on good and soft ground is mixed, and the step up to 3m1f is a query, but he has the physical profile to dictate here.

runners_data.name: Rememberwhat
runners_data.note: Lightly raced six-year-old with just two recorded runs, both showing placed or midfield efforts at shorter trips on good ground; ridden by a 7lb claimer, trainer P G Fahey has no recent runners flagged in the 14-day stats, and the step up to 3m1f is a significant unknown — maps to a prominent role which suits if the pace ahead burns hot.

runners_data.name: Pets Georgina
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 23f and 18f on good ground give her the strongest recent form in the race, and her hold-up profile is ideally placed behind a contested pace; ridden by J J Slevin who provides a significant jockey upgrade, with five from six runs on similar going including two wins — her consistent form profile and strong going record make her the logical beneficiary of this race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Rocky's Diamond and Olympic Man are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 3m1f trip at Kilbeggan, creating a genuinely contested pace on good ground. Rocky's Diamond, trained by Declan Queally who is in sharp form (3/7 over 14 days), is the higher-rated of the two at OR 148 and is likely to dominate that battle, while Olympic Man — ridden by a 5lb claimer and returning after 29 days — may be forced to race prominently rather than lead outright. The result is a race run at an honest, pressured gallop throughout, which historically at Kilbeggan's tight track stretches out races enough to expose stamina weaknesses in those who overextend early. This shape clearly favours hold-up horses who can track off the pace and pounce in the straight, with Pets Georgina and Drumgill both carrying that profile — though Pets Georgina's recent winning form at 23f and 18f on good ground makes her the most immediately well-placed to exploit a contested lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Diamond and Olympic Man press each other through the early stages, setting a pressured honest gallop that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn each other out, leaving the race to those who have settled off the pace and arrive with running in the straight; Kilbeggan's tight circuit ensures there is limited time to recover once the pace eases. Pets Georgina's back-to-back wins on good ground and Drumgill's hold-up profile both suit a contest decided from the rear of the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Rocky's Diamond Leads Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Olympic Man fails to sustain his challenge early and Rocky's Diamond takes full control to set a measured, controlled gallop.
scenarios.body: Rocky's Diamond dictates from the front at a pace of his own choosing, conserving enough energy to be competitive at the finish having softened the race rather than been forced into a burn-up; his higher OR of 148 and trainer form give him a class edge in this scenario. A lone, unchallenged front-runner at this trip on good ground can absolutely see out the race if the pace is right.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Lands Race
scenarios.trigger: If Rememberwhat travels prominently just off the early leaders and the pace burns out those ahead before the final flight.
scenarios.body: Rememberwhat, ridden by a 7lb claimer but holding solid placing form at 16-19f on good ground, benefits from sitting just behind a contested lead without expending early energy; with only 152lbs and an uncontested run into the straight, a clean round could yield a winning position. The drop in exposed form relative to rivals is a concern, but the tactical position is advantageous if the scenario unfolds.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Chaos — Errors Decide
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace causes jumping errors or fallers, reducing the race to a scramble home among survivors.
scenarios.body: Over 3m1f with two front-runners pressing, jumping under pressure becomes a factor; any error at a late hurdle could reshuffle the order entirely. Drumgill's form includes a pulled-up run and inconsistency, while Olympic Man's form string includes a fall — both runners could benefit or be eliminated depending on how the jumping holds up.

watchPoints.text: Rocky's Diamond and Olympic Man will fight for the lead from flag-fall — watch whether either concedes in the first half-mile, as the outcome of that duel largely determines the race shape.

Olympic Man has a fall in his recent form string (form: 6P5F-8) and will be jumping under pressure if pressed for the lead — a jumping error from him in the early stages could cause interference for runners tracking close behind.

Drumgill has a pulled-up run in recent form and inconsistent finishing positions; if the pace is not truly brutal enough to bring him into it from off the pace, his hold-up style may leave him too much to do at Kilbeggan's tight finish.

Pets Georgina is shouldering 150lbs with a strong jockey booking in J J Slevin — watch in-running whether Slevin opts to track the leaders or drop her in behind; her position at the third-last hurdle will be the key indicator of whether she is travelling well enough to challenge.

Rememberwhat is unproven beyond 19f (just two career runs) — watch how she travels on the bridle heading to the final circuit, as any signs of laboured jumping or loss of position before three out would confirm the trip is beyond her current scope.

races.name: Smiddys Pub Mullingar Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Kings Jet
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type who ran only six days ago — quick turnaround bears watching; has a place record on good ground in similar company but has posted two non-completions recently, and Ricky Doyle must nurse him through the trip without incident.

runners_data.name: Anodandawink
runners_data.note: Won and placed twice on good ground over 24f which matches today's conditions well; Peter Smithers claims 7lb which helps at the weights, and the horse's recent form string ending in a win gives it the most current form in the race, though it does fade late per the flag.

runners_data.name: Mistyburn
runners_data.note: Wears tongue-strap and headgear, and has shown consistent placing form on good ground at this distance range; though depicted in midfield, this is a true hold-up horse that will likely settle at the rear — the style displacement means it must produce a stronger-than-usual move from a long way back to factor.

runners_data.name: Zolpharine
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on good ground make the going ideal, and Daniel King rides for the same yard as The Little Yank which adds an interesting tactical dimension; the 71-day absence is the key question — if fit it has the highest ceiling in this field, but racing out of its natural hold-up role (shown in midfield) tempers confidence slightly.

runners_data.name: The Little Yank
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old whose natural style is prominent rather than front-running; placed on good ground at this trip last time out, it wears a hood and will likely set a gentle pace — but it is doing so against its natural instincts, and Michael Kenneally (5lb claim) must judge the tempo carefully to avoid burning it out over this demanding trip.

races.paceDynamic: The Little Yank, a natural prominent type redistributed to the front in this map, is the only horse likely to set any meaningful pace over this 3m1f trip at Kilbeggan, and with four hold-up horses behind, the race will be run at a controlled, modest gallop throughout. Good ground suits a clean-jumping, economical style, and with no genuine front runner to press The Little Yank, the pace is unlikely to be pressurised until late in the race. Zolpharine and Mistyburn are true hold-up types pushed into the midfield mapping because the rear of the field is congested — both are likely to race further back than shown, not closer to the pace. This shape strongly favours a horse who can travel smoothly off a steady tempo and produce a decisive late effort, making the hold-up, strong-finishing profile the one to side with — provided the horse has the class and fitness to quicken off an honest but unhurried early pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If The Little Yank sets an uncontested, modest gallop and the hold-up horses settle before producing sustained late runs.
scenarios.body: The Little Yank controls matters on a comfortable lead while the hold-up group track in behind, and when pressure arrives from the final fence the horses with the most recent form and class carry their momentum through to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Zolpharine Powers Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Zolpharine, returning from 71 days off but sharp on good ground, travels strongly and delivers an emphatic run under Daniel King.
scenarios.body: Zolpharine has back-to-back wins on good ground at this trip range and, if fit from the break, could assert from the home turn and outclass a modest field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Compounds, Stoics Win
scenarios.trigger: If The Little Yank's unnatural lead role costs it energy and it fades after the last, leaving a scrappy finish among the hold-up types.
scenarios.body: With no horse able to sustain the pace robustly, the race fragments late and the horse with the soundest jumping record and most reliable fitness claims a messy finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises on Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the small field produces jumping errors or fallers that disrupt the leading group and a fresh, well-handicapped horse seizes an unexpected opportunity.
scenarios.body: With only five runners any incident reshapes the race entirely, and a horse jumping cleanly through trouble could inherit a winning position without needing superior form.

watchPoints.text: The Little Yank's unnatural front-running role for Michael Kenneally (5) over 3m1f — if it sets too quick a pace or gets too lonely on the lead, it will compound before the last and reshape the entire race.
Zolpharine's 71-day layoff for John Patrick Ryan — it has the form to win but if it comes up underdone it will drop out tamely from the home turn, leaving Daniel King with little to work with.

Anodandawink is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — if the pace is truly sedate, the final jumping test may expose that tendency, particularly with a 7lb-claiming amateur in Peter Smithers aboard.

Kings Jet ran just six days ago — monitor early paddock behaviour and jumping for signs of fatigue or reluctance, as back-to-back runs in jumps company can expose horses quickly when the ground is on the faster side.

With only five runners any jumping error, particularly at the open ditches on the Kilbeggan circuit, could promote an otherwise out-of-form horse into a decisive position — clean rounds may matter more than raw class here.

races.name: KEPAK Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Jasko Des Dames
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner; Henry De Bromhead handler, Mike O'Connor aboard, Good ground fine, but a STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence — has competed at OR=130 and sets the pace here, though with no real rival to press him this may suit if he can be lobbed along comfortably.

runners_data.name: Ma Jacks Hill
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy is a major positive for this Gordon Elliott-trained 6-year-old, whose last three runs include a win and a place both over 20f on Good; a natural prominent type who should secure a berth just behind the leader without having to fight for it.

runners_data.name: A Law Of Her Own
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins's 9-year-old returns just 8 days after last run but has strong Good-ground form (14/15 similar-going runs in the frame), a recent win over 16f, and as a genuine hold-up type she is perfectly positioned to be delivered late in the dominant pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Intense Approach
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer who has struggled for consistency (5U50-0 recent form) but wears a hood and has the fitness edge of an 8-day turnaround; trainer John McConnell has 0 winners from 25 runners in the past 14 days, which is a concern alongside the moderate recent record.

runners_data.name: Mickie Angel
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes the ride on this Denis Gerard Hogan-trained 8-year-old, whose best form (three places in five runs) has come at trips around 20-22f; in truth a prominent racer by nature, he's been pushed to midfield on the map because this field cannot accommodate all the prominent types — his chance depends on getting a cleaner position than the pace map suggests.

runners_data.name: Rexem
runners_data.note: A consistent hold-up performer with five consecutive placed or in-contention finishes over 20f on Good ground — his natural rear-rank style is genuine, and the 5-lb claimer Josh Williamson is a factor to weigh, though his course form and going suitability (11/15) make him a legitimate late-running threat in the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Ceanndana
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's 9-year-old returns after 85 days off — the longest layoff in the field — wearing a hood; by nature a prominent type, he has been displaced to midfield on the map because there is simply no room for him at the front, and a sharp return from a significant break compounds the risk of a below-par first run back.

runners_data.name: Grange Walk
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old veteran wearing blinkers who has been nudged to midfield from his true hold-up position simply because the map is congested at the rear; Daniel King takes the ride for a trainer with no recent winners, and at OR=106 off a 15-day break, his best hope is an open, attrition-based race that delivers him a clear late run.

races.paceDynamic: Jasko Des Bromhead is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to press him from the jump, he should be able to control tempo on his own terms over this 2m4f trip on Good ground at Kilbeggan — a configuration that historically suits a horse that can settle comfortably in front and conserve energy through the middle stages. The redistribution flag matters: Mickie Angel, Ceanndana, and Grange Walk are all natural prominent or hold-up types who cannot all claim their preferred position, meaning the prominent berths directly behind Jasko Des Dames will be contested early, injecting a degree of scrimmaging that could compromise those horses' rhythm without meaningfully quickening the overall tempo. Ma Jacks Hill and Intense Approach are the other natural prominent types who will look to sit just off the pace, and their ability to track comfortably without being squeezed out is a key tactical variable. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a sustainable gallop on Good ground — most clearly favours hold-up horses with class and a clean passage, particularly A Law Of Her Own and Rexem, both of whom are true hold-up types with strong form at this trip on this going and will arrive late having avoided the scrimmage for prominent positions. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all get their natural position; Jasko Des Dames is overwhelmingly likely to secure the lead, with Ma Jacks Hill and Intense Approach best-placed to claim the prominent slots behind, at the expense of the redistributed Mickie Angel and Ceanndana.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jasko Leads, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Jasko Des Dames sets a controlled, uncontested pace and the prominent scrimmage behind him burns off Mickie Angel and Ceanndana early.
scenarios.body: Jasko Des Dames rolls along in front at a sound but measured gallop, and the hold-up horses A Law Of Her Own and Rexem, travelling well in rear, produce their runs from the final bend to cut him down.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Jasko Des Dames steals a significant enough advantage early and the prominent scrimmage behind stifles any clean pursuit from the closers.
scenarios.body: The pace is sustainable enough that Jasko Des Dames, never headed and never truly tested, simply keeps finding on the flat to repel challengers who have used energy to get into position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Ma Jacks Hill or Intense Approach travel supremely well just off Jasko Des Dames and strike from the second-last with enough class to hold the closers.
scenarios.body: The Good ground and the manageable pace suits a horse that can sit second or third without fuss and produce a long, sustained run from the turn, denying the hold-up horses a clean run of momentum.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles Result
scenarios.trigger: If the early contest for prominent positions causes interference or falls that reshuffle the field entirely and open the race up for an unconsidered runner.
scenarios.body: Grange Walk, a genuine hold-up type who has been mapped to midfield due to overcrowding, may benefit most if the field thins dramatically and a clean late run becomes available.

watchPoints.text: Mickie Angel and Ceanndana are both natural prominent types who cannot hold that position — watch for early crowding and shuffling from the third to fifth places as they and Ma Jacks Hill and Intense Approach all seek the same berths behind Jasko Des Dames in the first mile.

Ceanndana returns after 85 days off and has been reassigned from his preferred prominent role — if he needs the run and gets into trouble early, Sean Flanagan may face a difficult decision about whether to push or settle, potentially causing interference.

Rexem's rider Josh Williamson is a 5-lb claimer on only his second Kilbeggan appearance — watch whether the inexperience of the partnership allows gaps to close or the horse to lose his position at a critical late fence.

A Law Of Her Own runs for the second time in 8 days — monitor her energy levels in the final half-mile; if she travels with her usual fluency she is the primary threat to the leader, but any sign of laboured jumping under fatigue would undermine the hold-up scenario significantly.

Grange Walk has fallen or been brought down in two of his last six starts (B marker in form) — watch his jumping at the early fences, as any loose horse or exit from the field will immediately alter the tactical shape and the ability of closers to deliver clean late runs.
